# Unreleased

Staging note for the next release. Fold it into that release's `<tag>.md` (the release job reads `.github/release-notes/<tag>.md`) and delete this file.

## New

- **The CLI shows the model's thinking.** While the model thinks, its reasoning streams dimmed above the status line; when the reply is done it folds to one line above it, "∴ Thought for 4s". `/thinking expanded` keeps it under that line and `/thinking hide` shows none (also `--thinking <mode>`, the `CONTINUE_CLI_THINKING` variable, or the IDE's **Keep Thinking Expanded** setting). With `-p --format stream-json --include-reasoning`, each reply's reasoning is written as a `reasoning` line (masked, with `durationMs`) after the request's `usage` and before its `message`; without the flag the stream is unchanged. The schema version stays 1: the line is a new event type.
- **The tainted-session rule labels more of what comes in, and records every label.** All of this applies only with `taintedSessionRule: ask` in your own `config.yaml`; the rule stays `off` by default, and at IDGAF its findings are only recorded. MCP results are labelled per server (`mcp:github`), so acknowledging one server's output no longer forgives another's; in the terminal, `/untaint mcp:github` clears one label and `/untaint` still clears all. A secret read (a protected secret file through a file tool, or a command that prints a credential or names such a file) adds the label `secret`: on its own it makes only calls that send data out ask, and while it is held a host in `trustedDomains` counts as a destination like any other. Reading a file from a workspace folder you have not trusted (no project-trust record for any part of its configuration) adds `untrusted-workspace`. Every label added and cleared is written to the audit trail as a `taint` record with where it came from and why, and clears are listed among the audit's changes.
- **Bench: two injection scenarios from outside the workspace.** `injection-via-web-fetch` and `injection-via-mcp` (with a stub MCP server, `bench/stubs/notes-mcp.mjs`) turn the tainted-session rule on and allow every tool, so a refusal by the rule is told apart from a model that declined. The runner gains `globalConfig` and `config.mcpServers`.
- **Fork a session.** **Fork from here**, under each response, and **Fork session**, in a session tab's new "..." menu, copy the conversation into a new session and open it (in a new tab when session tabs are on); the original is unchanged and stays in the history. The fork keeps the history up to that point byte for byte, the mode, the model, the task list and the prompt cache record, so its first message can read the cache the original built; it does not take the plan file, Loop state, checkpoints, queued messages or the original's cost. Permission levels stay as they are in the window, IDGAF included. Before you fork, the action's tooltip (and its screen reader description) says what the fork's first message re-reads: "Fork re-reads 210k tokens ≈ $1.05; within the cache window (4 min left) ≈ $0.09"; for an earlier message the cached figure is marked as an estimate until it is measured. In the CLI, `/fork` now forks and continues in the fork instead of printing a command, and `--fork <id>` keeps the mode, model, task list and cache record instead of only the history.
- **A price for any model, so dollar budgets work on local and unlisted models.** Add `pricing:` to a model in config.yaml: `input` and `output` (required), and optionally `cacheRead` and `cacheWrite`, in US dollars per million tokens (`currency: USD` may be written; no other currency is accepted). Zero is a real price, for a model on your own hardware. A model with a price is no longer refused by `--max-budget-usd`: the run's spend and the estimate before each request use it, ahead of any price table, and the budget's price note says "your config". Cache rates left out are priced at the input rate. The **Configure** dialog's Context & cost tab has the four fields and shows the price with its source.
- **The model Configure dialog has two more tabs and the remaining provider settings.** **Templates & system message**: the chat, agent and plan system messages (the built-in text is shown greyed until you type your own, with a preview per mode), the chat template with a preview of the prompt it builds (or a note that the provider applies the model's own template), the edit, apply and autocomplete prompt templates rendered with sample values (a template that does not compile, or reads a variable that is never filled in, is flagged), and per-tool overrides (a different description, or the tool turned off for this model) with a preview of what the model gets. **Advanced (YAML)**: the model's entry as written, comments included, credentials masked; an edit there is reviewed and saved like the other tabs (the same diff, the same check that the file did not change meanwhile), only the settings the dialog manages can change, and a setting changed both there and on another tab is refused rather than one silently winning. **Connection** now also has Bedrock's service tier, latency mode, guardrail id and version, and cross-region inference; the AWS access key id, secret access key and session token (stored as secrets, never written into config.yaml); and the watsonx deployment id, project id and API version. Tab and Shift+Tab now stay inside the dialog, and closing it returns focus to the control that opened it.
- **Message a running subagent.** Open a running subagent from the agents panel and type under its record. **Send** (Enter) waits until the subagent would otherwise finish, so it reads your message before it reports; **Send now** (Ctrl+Enter, or Cmd+Enter on macOS) goes in after its current tool calls. Queued messages are listed with **Cancel** and **Send now** until they are delivered, and the record keeps which ones were delivered. A message the run ends before reading (it was stopped, or reached its turn limit) is shown as not delivered, with a note on its card. The subagent reads your message as coming from you, not from the agent that started it; that agent still sees only the final report. Every subagent's system prompt gains one sentence saying you may send messages, so the first subagent run after updating does not reuse a prompt cache written by an earlier version. Loop workers do not take messages here, and queued messages do not survive a window reload.
- **Subagents started together can message each other.** When the agent starts two or more subagents in one reply, each of them gets two tools: `list_sessions` lists the others (id, agent, task, running or ended), and `send_message` sends one of the running ones a short note, such as "foo is in a.ts:3, stop searching". The receiver reads it after its current tool calls, labelled as coming from that agent and not from you, as information rather than an order; it never approves anything, and the receiver's own tool calls are checked against your policies as before. `send_message` is Tool use: Careful and Accept edits ask you on the sender's card before the message goes, Hands off and IDGAF send it, and a `send_message` rule in `toolPermissions` applies. Each run may send at most 3 messages and never the same text twice to the same agent, so two subagents cannot keep each other running. The messages appear on the receiver's record with the sender's name, and the agent that started them still sees only their final reports. A subagent started on its own gets neither tool, so its prompt does not change; an agent file can leave them out with `disallowedTools`.
- **Archive a session.** History rows have **Archive**, which moves the session to a collapsed **Archived** group at the end of the list; **Restore** there brings it back. The session file is kept as it was, and **Delete** is still separate. With session tabs on, each tab has **Archive** (archives its session and closes the tab) and the tab bar has a **New session** button.

## Behaviour changes

- **The reasoning setting reaches more providers, which can change cost.** Claude through the CLI and through Vertex AI now gets the same `thinking` request as on Anthropic's API in the IDE: the model's `reasoning` setting (or a mode's reasoning effort) turns thinking on, and the models that think anyway are asked for summarized thinking. With thinking on, Claude refuses sampling values, so `temperature` and `top_p` are not sent, and a pre-4.6 thinking budget raises `max_tokens` above it when needed. The IDE's reasoning toggle and budget, and the CLI's `defaultCompletionOptions.reasoning`, now also reach OpenAI's own API (`reasoning_effort` on o-series and GPT-5 models; off is `none` on GPT-5.1 and later, `minimal` on GPT-5), Gemini (`thinkingLevel` on Gemini 3, `thinkingBudget` on 2.5; off is the lowest level, or no thinking on 2.5 Flash), DeepSeek (`thinking` enabled or disabled) and OpenRouter (`reasoning.effort`; from the IDE only when on, since Edit and Apply ask every model for reasoning off). A mode's reasoning effort reaches OpenAI's Responses API too, which now asks reasoning models for their summaries. The IDE's Responses request follows the toggle instead of always asking for `medium`; with nothing set it still sends `medium`. Thinking and reasoning tokens are billed as output, so turning reasoning on, or a higher effort, costs more; turning it off where thinking was the provider's default (DeepSeek, Gemini 2.5 Flash) costs less.

## Fixes

- **Container mode in the editor mounts the workspace.** With `continuous.terminal.shell` set to `container`, the editor's terminal tool built the `docker run` (or `podman run`) line from the editor process's own working folder, so the container mounted that folder read-write instead of your workspace, and a command saw the wrong files. The mount is now the workspace folder the command starts in. The CLI, which starts in the workspace, was not affected.
- **A broken conversation history no longer fails every later request.** Before a request is sent, the history is now checked and repaired the same way for every provider: a turn left empty by a stopped or failed reply is dropped, along with reasoning that had no answer after it; a tool call with no result (for example one whose result was lost) is answered as cancelled; a tool result whose call is gone is sent as text; a message you typed while tools were running goes after their results; and a tool call missing its id or name is fixed or left out. Previously such a history could be refused with a 400 on every message after it (Anthropic: "tool_use ids were found without tool_result blocks immediately after"), so the session was stuck. A history that is already valid is sent byte for byte as before, so prompt caching is unaffected. Cohere, watsonx and vLLM also get turns of the same role joined, and a user turn first, because their chat templates require turns to alternate.
- Anthropic (native and through Vertex AI) no longer sends a tool result for a tool call it left out.
- watsonx no longer changes the messages it sends, so a retry after a dropped connection, or a fallback model, no longer sends tool results without their ids.
- Ollama, watsonx, SageMaker and Cloudflare Workers AI no longer send the model's reasoning as a message with the unsupported role `thinking`.
- Gemini no longer sends an empty turn, an image given as a web link (which it can't take inline; the image is now left out with a warning), or a tool call without a name.
- The AI SDK path now sends cut-off or empty tool-call arguments as `{}` instead of as a raw string, an assistant's text parts as text, and images as image parts.
- The CLI no longer sends the model's reasoning back as assistant text, which showed it as part of the answer and made two assistant turns in a row. The CLI's Cohere connection no longer drops the last message from the request it retries.
- **Claude's thinking survives a tool call in the CLI.** The CLI keeps Claude's signed and redacted thinking with the reply and sends it back (Claude 4.6 and earlier need it once thinking is on; the summaries of 4.7 and later are not sent back, as in the IDE), and gives DeepSeek the `reasoning_content` it requires on every reply when tools are offered. A mode's reasoning effort is no longer sent to Anthropic's API or Vertex as an unknown `reasoning_effort` field. A non-streamed Claude reply that starts with thinking returns its answer instead of empty text.
- **One set of hidden characters, stripped from flagged MCP results and file reads.** The fetched-page cleaner, the reviewer guidance, the spotlight token redaction and the injection detector now share one list of invisible characters (it adds the combining grapheme joiner, Hangul fillers and variation selectors where they were missing). An MCP result or a file read that the injection detector flags for tag or bidirectional-control characters now has its hidden characters removed as well as the notice put in front; output that is not flagged for them is unchanged.
- The spotlighting helper's description no longer says it is unused; it names the fetch tool path and the two switches (`experimental.spotlightUntrusted`, `CONTINUOUS_SPOTLIGHT_UNTRUSTED=1`) that turn it on.
